comment: Questions with known answers, run against the live assistant after every
deploy. Each case says what the reply must contain and — more importantly —
The 'mustNot' half is the point. Anyone can write a prompt telling a model
not to invent things; only a test catches it when it does anyway. Every
case here with a 'mustNot' is a real mistake the assistant made once.
Assertions are on facts, never on phrasing — the wording will differ every
run and a suite that fails on wording gets ignored.

A caveat learned the hard way: assert on the CLAIM, not on a word. 'loan player' was forbidden outright, and then a perfectly correct answer — 'the rule book sets out no process for loaning players' — failed the suite. A test that fails on right answers is worse than no test, because people stop believing it.

Cases may be a single 'ask' or a full 'conversation'. The multi-turn ones matter more than they look: the assistant defends its own earlier answers, so a stale saved chat can drag a corrected prompt back into a mistake.

Second time bitten by the same thing: match on meaning with tolerant patterns. 'double-chance' did not match 'double chance', and forbidding '48 hours' outright failed an answer that correctly said seniors have no such process while juniors do. Prefer a loose alternation over an exact phrase, and scope a mustNot to the claim you actually object to.

cases.name: fill-in second game
cases.ask: Can a fill-in player play a second game?
cases.why: A PlayHQ fill-in covers the first game only; after that they must be registered.

cases.name: a senior exemption is exceptional, not a process
cases.ask: How do I request a dispensation for a senior finals game?
cases.why: The President confirmed on 3 Sep 2026 that senior finals exemptions do exist, in exceptional circumstances, so a flat denial is now wrong. What stays wrong is presenting one as a process: the senior book sets out no form, no route and no deadline, and the assistant once invented one by lifting the junior book's deadlines. Asserts the answer names the committee and conveys the high bar. The banned patterns are the two ways a deadline gets invented: the junior 48 hours pinned to seniors, and an instruction to submit by a time. An earlier version banned 5 PM near Thursday anywhere in the reply, which failed one run in three -- proximity to a fact is not a claim, and a sentence saying the junior deadline does NOT apply reads identically to a mustNot.

cases.name: junior dispensation deadline
cases.ask: What is the deadline to request a junior dispensation or exception?
cases.why: The junior book carries two deadlines — 5 PM Thursday before the game in the contacts table, and 48 hours before the match for committee exceptions under Finals Eligibility. Either is a fair answer; inventing a third is not.

cases.name: borrowing players for finals
cases.ask: Can I borrow a player from another team at my club for a final?
cases.why: Nothing in the senior book describes loaning players. It once said you could. The assertion targets an affirmative permission, not the word itself — a correct denial says 'loan' too.

cases.name: U15 innings end
cases.ask: How many wickets end a U15 innings?
cases.why: U15: 10 wickets, unlike U11 and U13.

cases.name: revised target, no plus one
cases.ask: Team A scored 175 in 35 overs. The second innings is cut to 15 overs. What is the revised target?
cases.why: MCA uses revised overs x run rate. It once applied the usual cricket +1 convention, which MCA does not use.

cases.name: umpire fee T35
cases.ask: What is the umpire fee for T35?
cases.why: $85 per team.

cases.name: T20 powerplay
cases.ask: How many powerplay overs in T20?
cases.why: First 6 overs, mandatory.

cases.name: league washout has no reserve day
cases.ask: Our league game was washed out. When is the reserve day?
cases.why: League games washed out share the points; only finals have reserve days.

cases.name: team count
cases.ask: How many teams play in MCA this season?
cases.why: 86 teams, matching the PlayHQ ladders.

cases.name: falls back to the MCC Laws
cases.ask: What counts as obstructing the field?
cases.why: Not specified by MCA, so the Laws apply — the senior book says so.

cases.name: contact section exists
cases.ask: Give me the website link for contacts
cases.why: The site has a contact section. It once denied that.

cases.name: admits when it does not know
cases.ask: What is the MCA policy on drone photography at grounds?
cases.why: Nothing in either book covers this. It must say so rather than invent a policy.

cases.name: does not defend its own earlier mistake

conversation.content: Two of my players are unavailable for the 5 Sept final and one is injured. Can I get eligible players from another team at my club playing MCA 10 rounds in a different grade?

🏆 **What You Can Do**
✅ **Loan players:** You can use loan players from other teams at your club, provided they meet the eligibility rule above.

**Request a Dispensation**
If you have extenuating circumstances you can request a dispensation from the association:
Email: melbournecricketassociation@gmail.com
Deadline: At least 48 hours before the match
Can you explain the loan player and dispensation options again?

mustNot: (you|your (side|team|club)) (can|may|could|should|must|need to|are able to) (request|apply for|submit|seek) a dispensation[^.]{0,60}(48 hours|thursday)
cases.why: A saved conversation used to carry an old wrong answer back into the prompt, and the assistant stayed consistent with itself rather than with the rule book — inventing a loan eligibility rule to justify what it had said earlier. Single-turn tests missed this entirely, which is how the fix looked complete when it was not.

cases.name: all junior grades have finals
cases.ask: Are there finals for juniors?
cases.why: It told a parent U11 A was league only. Every junior grade has finals — the rule book says Top 4, and PlayHQ has three finals rounds for all four grades. It also volunteered the committee-exceptions clause unprompted, which makes an edge case look like part of the ordinary rule. The double-chance format was moved to its own case: demanding it here fought the rule that says answer the question and stop.

cases.name: junior finals dates
cases.ask: When are the junior finals played?
cases.why: Finals Round 1 on 6 Sep, Preliminary Final 13 Sep, Grand Final 20 Sep, every junior grade.

cases.name: junior finals qualification
cases.ask: How many games does a junior need to play to qualify for finals?
cases.why: Minimum 3 home-and-away matches for that team, and more games for that team than any other in the age group.

cases.name: quotes a section under its own heading
cases.ask: What are the U15 leg-side wide rules?
cases.why: The heading rows inside the book's tables were being flattened into data rows, so the whole Detailed Rules section read as though it sat under 'Batter Retirement'. The assistant repeated that heading over no-ball content.

cases.name: raises the exception when it is actually needed
cases.ask: One of my U13 players has only played 2 games because two rounds were washed out. Can he still play in the finals?
cases.why: The counterpart to the finals case. That one fails if exceptions are volunteered unasked; this one fails if they are withheld from someone who needs them — a player short of games through washouts, which is the book's own worked example. Restraint must not turn into silence.

cases.name: T35 fee includes MoM awards
cases.ask: What is included in the $425 Saturday T35 registration fee?
cases.why: The $425 is Registration $175 + MoM $125 + Finals Awards $125. It once listed MoM as a T20-and-10-rounds-only component, which does not add up to $425.

cases.name: chasing team batting on is in the book
cases.ask: In U13, does the team batting second have to stop once they pass the target, or can they bat out their overs?
cases.why: The junior book says under Wickets & Dismissals: 'The chasing team, if the wicket cap has not been reached, may bat its full allocation of overs.' It told a club captain the books were silent and settled it from the MCC Laws instead, because the sentence sits mid-row in a long U11 & U13 table cell.

cases.name: does not rule against the umpire
cases.ask: Our umpires keep stopping the game as soon as we pass the target, but MCA told us at the start of the season that the side batting second must play out the full 30 overs. Who is right?
must: full quota|full allocation|even after the (result|target)|play(s|ing)? (it |them |their )?out|all (30|thirty) overs
cases.why: Anik Malik asked this and was told his umpires were right and MCA's own briefing was wrong advice. Both halves were false: the committee adopted the U15 rule early in Winter 2026 and PlayHQ is set to match. 30 overs names the grade, so there is an answer to give.

cases.name: junior loan player comes from the opposition
cases.ask: In U13, can I borrow a player from another team at my club if we are short?
must: opposition|other team on the day|team you are playing
cases.why: The book says loan players apply 'when one team is short and the opposition has surplus' — lent by the opposition on the day. It has repeatedly rebuilt this as borrowing from another team at your club, gated on the 3-game finals qualification rule, which is not a loan condition anywhere in the book.

cases.name: U11 innings runs to the full overs
cases.ask: In U11, does the side batting second stop as soon as they pass the target?
must: all allocated overs are bowled|full ball allocation|full allocation of overs
cases.why: The U11 rule reads 'All batters face their full ball allocation, and the innings concludes when all allocated overs are bowled' — the innings is defined by the overs running out, not the target being passed. It told a club 'for U11, the rule book is silent on this point', which is the opposite of what the book says.

cases.name: U15 chase plays out its overs
cases.ask: In U15, does the game stop as soon as the chasing team passes the target?
must: full quota|full allocation|even after the (result|target)|play(s|ing)? (it |them |their )?out|all (30|thirty) overs
cases.why: The committee adopted this early in Winter 2026 and PlayHQ has 'continue scoring when target total reached' switched on for U15. It is not in the rule book, so the assistant used to answer it from the MCC Laws and got it backwards — telling a club its umpires were right to stop play.

cases.name: junior finals format
cases.ask: What is the finals format for U13 — how do the three weeks work?
cases.why: PlayHQ standard: the top two get the double chance. Asked plainly it should say so — this is the question that question is for, whereas 'are there finals?' is answered by yes, which grades, and who qualifies.

cases.name: finals games do not add up across grades
cases.ask: I've played 3 games in T35 10 Rounds C Grade and 1 game in B Grade this season. Am I eligible for the C Grade finals?
cases.why: The committee's reading: the one-grade rule picks the grade first, then the minimum is measured in that grade alone. Games are not accumulated across grades — 3 in C plus 1 in B is 3, not 4. It is the rule most likely to be argued over at a finals deadline, and it is nowhere in the rule book. The must patterns accept a leading No as the denial: the reply that failed this case opened "No - you need 4 qualifying games in C Grade alone, and you have 3", which is the clearest possible way to say it and matched none of the longer phrasings. Same lesson the shared DENIES macro already learned.

cases.name: senior knockouts have two umpires
cases.ask: What is the umpire fee for a T35 semi-final?
cases.why: The seniors book says two umpires are provided for Pre-semis, Semi-Finals and Finals, and teams pay for both. Quoting the $85 league rate alone sends a captain to a semi-final with half the money.
